note: Rules for the dish lookup (INDB plan, phase 3). Every number here is my proposal from the phase 2 comparison with INDB (indb_phase2/PHASE2_REPORT.md); a dietitian confirms or changes them before production.

calculated_dishes.note: Path B: a dish that is in INDB but not in the library is calculated from its ingredients, and only when every ingredient has a value (coverage 1.0). It is always labelled an estimate and given as a range.

range_percent.note: 15% covered 96% of the 847 fully calculated INDB recipes, 25% covered 99%. Meat and fish dishes drifted most (chicken -23%, mutton -20% median).

meat_fish_note: First letter of the INDB ingredient code. N = poultry, O = meat, P = fish, as seen in codes N003 chicken, O064 mutton, P057 pomfret.

plausibility.note: A value above a limit is never shown. 900 kcal per 100 g is pure fat; 1,500 kcal is more than most people eat in a whole meal. Dishes calculated from ingredients (path B) use 1,000 because INDB's own serving data is least reliable there, and a serving counted in pieces (a piece of mathri, a slice of cake) is limited to 400 kcal per piece: INDB has 'one piece' of mathri at 1,182 kcal and 'two uttapam' at 1,295 kcal, which are data errors. INDB has 108 recipes above 1,000 kcal per serving.

generic_words_note: A word that only describes a dish, never names one. INDB writes '(vegetarian)' or '(dry)' after dish names, so the alias table has 'vegetarian' as an alias of two different dishes; 'calories in vegetarian biryani' was answered with 'Shepherd's pie or Dhansak'. A run of words made only of these is never taken as a dish name.
